output.answer_markdown: Palo Alto Networks says significant seasonal factors may cause its second and fourth fiscal quarters to record greater revenue sequentially than its first and third fiscal quarters [1]. One factor is that end-customers with a December 31 fiscal year-end spend remaining unused discretionary budgets before year-end, which potentially boosts second-quarter revenue [2]. Another is that sales compensation plans, structured around annual quotas and commission rate accelerators, potentially boost fourth-quarter revenue [3]. Seasonal reductions in business activity during August in the United States, Europe and certain other regions potentially hurt first-quarter revenue [4]. Finally, the timing of end-customer budget planning at the beginning of the calendar year can delay spending and potentially hurt third-quarter revenue [5].
